chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan from his father from Ibn al-Mughira from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father from Ali (peace be upon him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"Whoever testifies before us and then changes [his testimony], we take hold of him with the first [testimony] and discard the last."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a witness who changes their testimony in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the Imams from Imam Ali (AS), establishes the principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity) in judicial testimony, where the initial statement is deemed more reliable than a subsequent alteration. In Shia jurisprudence, this supports the view that a witness's first account holds precedence unless proven false by other evidence, ensuring stability in legal proceedings. It highlights the Prophet's authority in defining evidentiary standards, linking directly to the Imams' role as interpreters of divine law.
